text:
Tyler Bertuzzi had two goals and an assist in Chicago's 6-3 win over Toronto on Tuesday, and it fit his role: the veteran net-front presence on a young Blackhawks team, now on the top power-play unit. He's at 5 goals and 10 points in 22 games, scoring right about what his chances deserve (5 goals on 4.5 expected).

The five-on-five numbers aren't kind. Chicago gets only 40% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, and his recent stretch (5 points in ten against 5.6 expected) is ordinary. The Blackhawks have been losing more than winning, and the injury to Connor Bedard, which Mark Lazerus called the big story of that Toronto night, puts more on everyone.

Evolving-Hockey offers context worth keeping in mind. Last season they had him 20th among 401 forwards in wins above replacement while playing with the weakest teammates in the league by their impact (bottom 1%). That's a player whose raw numbers understate him. Watch the net front: Scott Powers noted him screening the goalie on a Frank Nazar goal, the kind of work that never shows up in his own line.
headline: Bertuzzi is doing his job on a young team
